summary.text: Provided Teams snippets show refresh-link lookup, access_denied-as-removed handling, and token-dict key handling that need narrow fixes; no tests or tools were run.

facts.text: Refresh loads SourceReference by primary-key get with evidence_id, while import creates SourceReference with evidence_id as a field; if the PK is not evidence_id this lookup can miss and incorrectly return 404.
Refresh maps access_denied to missing=True and then marks the evidence removed, conflating an authorization failure with source deletion.
Refresh write transaction dereferences item.removed without checking for None, so concurrent deletion could cause an unhandled error instead of a clean 404/409.
Token refresh indexes fresh and cached token dicts directly; missing refresh_token/scope keys would raise KeyError instead of returning a reconnect error.
Access path reads tenant_id and expires_at with direct indexing, so malformed stored tokens can raise KeyError/TypeError instead of a controlled 401 reconnect.
Import validates chat_id with anchored pattern while read_chat uses an unanchored pattern, making refresh-time validation inconsistent with import-time validation.
Refresh checks grant mismatch before the write transaction but does not re-validate the link/grant inside the locked write transaction, leaving a stale-read window.

next_steps.text: Plan to replace the refresh lookup with an evidence_id-column query and re-fetch the link inside the locked write transaction.
Plan to keep access_denied as an error via failure() and only mark removed for positively confirmed deletion/empty cases.
Plan to add explicit None handling after the second Evidence fetch before checking removed status.
Plan to use defensive .get() access for refreshed and cached token fields and raise reconnect on missing/invalid token shape.
Plan to align refresh-time chat validation with the anchored import pattern.

brief.draft:
Subject: Teams connector review — authorization and refresh findings

Scope: review only of the provided own-code snippets. No tests or tools were run.

Findings from the snippets:
1. Refresh loads the link with `ref = session.get(SourceReference, evidence_id)` and never re-loads it inside the write transaction. Please query by evidence_id column and re-check inside the locked transaction.
2. Refresh treats `if exc.code in ("access_denied", "source_unavailable", "source_empty"):` as `missing = True` and then sets `item.removed = True`. For access_denied this conflates a permission failure with deletion. Please keep access_denied as an error and only mark removed for confirmed deletion/empty.
3. Second write transaction does `item = session.get(Evidence, evidence_id, populate_existing=True)` then `if item.removed:` without a None check. Please handle concurrently deleted evidence explicitly.
4. Token refresh does `fresh["refresh_token"] = fresh["refresh_token"] or tokens["refresh_token"]` and `fresh["scope"] = fresh["scope"] or tokens["scope"]`, plus direct `tokens["tenant_id"]`, `tokens["expires_at"]`, `tokens["scope"]` reads. Missing keys would raise KeyError instead of a reconnect error. Please use defensive gets and validate.
5. Chat ID validation differs: import uses `pattern=r"^19:[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]+$"` while refresh path uses `identifier(chat_id, r"19:[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]+")` without anchors. Please use the same anchored validation in both paths.

Suggested next: confirm SourceReference primary-key/lookup, grant() expected-grant semantics, and identifier() matching semantics, then patch the items above.
